goldCandidates.q: [Eval-Gold-01] An annuity pays ${pmt} at the BEGINNING of each year for {n} years. At an effective annual discount rate of {r}%, what is the present value today?
w: Used ordinary annuity formula instead of annuity-due (1 + r) multiplier.

goldCandidates.q: [Eval-Gold-02] A distributor holds identical electronic components at year-end with historical cost of $50/unit. Under IFRS, estimated selling price is $54, completion cost is $3, and selling cost is $4. Under US GAAP (LIFO), replacement cost is $45, selling price minus selling cost is $50, and normal profit margin is $6. What carrying value per unit is reported under IFRS vs. US GAAP?
goldCandidates.ok: IFRS carries at $47 (NRV); US GAAP (LIFO) carries at $45 (replacement cost lies between NRV $50 and NRV − normal profit $44)
w: IFRS carries at $45; US GAAP carries at $47
Swapped IFRS NRV rule and US GAAP LIFO lower-of-cost-or-market rule.
Both IFRS and US GAAP carry at $50 historical cost
Market/NRV below $50 triggers write-down under both frameworks.
goldCandidates.sol: IFRS NRV = 54 − 3 − 4 = $47 < $50 → $47. US GAAP market = mid(replacement $45, ceiling $50, floor $44) = $45 < $50 → $45.
goldCandidates.difficultyRationale: Tests precise IFRS NRV vs. US GAAP LIFO LCM framework distinction.

goldCandidates.q: [Eval-Gold-03] An investment-bank research analyst covers a biotech issuer that offers to fly her and her spouse first-class to a resort conference. Her compliance officer states she may attend if the analyst discloses the trip in her next research note. Under Standard I(B) Independence and Objectivity, what is the proper conclusion?
goldCandidates.ok: She must decline the trip; disclosure does not cure accepting lavish issuer-funded travel that threatens objectivity
w: She may accept so long as her next report discloses the trip in bold text
Disclosure cannot legitimize gifts or hospitality from covered issuers that impair independence.
She may accept only if she rates the stock Sell afterward
A subsequent rating does not cure accepting an impairing benefit.
goldCandidates.sol: Standard I(B) requires refusing benefits that could reasonably compromise independence; compliance sign-off on disclosure cannot override the Standard.
goldCandidates.difficultyRationale: Tests Standard I(B) non-curability by disclosure.

goldCandidates.q: [Eval-Gold-04] The 1-year spot rate is {z1}% and the 2-year spot rate is {z2}% (annual compounding). What is the implied 1-year forward rate 1 year from today?
w: Used linear approximation (7.00%) instead of exact geometric compounding (7.02%).
Averaged the two spot rates instead of extracting the forward rate.
goldCandidates.difficultyRationale: Tests exact forward-rate compounding vs. linear approximation.
